_about: Newbury for tools/course/real/layout.py. Ring 0 = OSM's outer edge of the turf (point numbers on reference/newbury/plan-draft.png, lower panel). OSM's turf is about 55 m wide round the loop: the flat course outside and the jumps course inside, so the flat course's inside rail is taken 30 m in from the outer edge (offset 30). The spur at the far end (the round mile's chute) is narrow, so there the inside rail is its own west edge. Where the round course comes off the far bend it runs diagonally (north-west) into the straight course's inner side; the game's run-in is shared with the straight mile on the stands side, the round course's rail carrying on its diagonal into it. The 1m5f61y chute off the home bend is narrow: its inside rail starts 10 m in from its south edge.

stands._about: Newbury's stands, owner 18 Nov 19:38-19:39: 'same basic model' (as Doncaster) on his marked-up satellite view (1 the stand at the bend, angled; 2 the long stand, turned a little to look up the straight; 3 the stand beyond it, square on; 4 an area up the course on the stand side; 'festival' the infield opposite, along the inside rail from the bend up the course) and his old photo of Newbury's stands ('bit more pitched roof terrace etc': a brick block with a hipped roof, a long pitched-roof stand, and a separate roof-terrace stand with a little lookout pavilion on its roof). So: 1 the pitched-roof (gable) stand turned 45 to the run-in, 14 m off the turf; 2 the clock house (the brick block) and a second pitched-roof stand in one line turned 20, its left end on the front line; 3 low terraces and the roof-terrace stand with Rowley's little Victorian pavilion on its roof as the lookout. 4 is the stand-side festival zone (perimeter.festivals). Owner's mark-up on the plan, 19:42: 2 and 3 square on and set back (fronts about 65 m off the inside rail, as the real stands), in his boxes x -26..49 and 76..148; 4 the stand-side festival zone set back the same, x 170..377; 1 as it was. Owner, 21:25: 'Victorian pavilion, old pavilion, tiered stand and big pavilion maybe good for Newbury?': 1 the tiered stand (turned to the run-in); 2 the clock house and York's big pavilion; 3 the Park kit's Victorian pavilion and old pavilion. The pitched-roof stands and the roof-terrace stand with its lookout stood down (the lookout composite kept in the file). Owner, 21:26, with an old colour postcard of the stand: 'I would like to get these roof structures in there': a roof-terrace stand with a pavilion block and flagpole in the middle of its roof and a little hipped-roof lookout at one end (park_roof_terrace_stand_postcard: the Park old pavilion x0.45 and a site-props flagpole in the middle of the back block's roof, Rowley's Victorian pavilion x0.7 at the end), in area 3 between the Victorian pavilion and the old pavilion; area 3 runs on to x 187 and his area 4 (the stand-side festival) moves up to x 200. Owner, 21:51, from the numbered crib sheet, left to right: 'victorian pavilion, big pavilion, grand pavilion, rowley stand. and the roof structures should be on the grand pavilion and rowley stand as per the image': 1 at the bend the Park Victorian pavilion with towers (crib 7), turned to the run-in; 2 York's big pavilion (16) and Ascot's grand pavilion module (35); 3 the Rowley Mile's Rowley stand (26). The postcard's roof pieces split between the two as in the postcard, left to right: the pavilion block with its flagpole on the grand pavilion's ridge, the hipped-roof lookout (crib 28) at the right-hand end of the Rowley stand's roof. Area 3 runs to x 186 (the Rowley stand is 110 m); his area 4 stays at x 200..400. Owner, 22:15: 'split the 2 and 3 and then join 3 to 4. I would then make 3 and 4 kind of half and half of each across the length': a 15 m gap between the big pavilion and the grand pavilion; the grand pavilion joined to the Rowley stand in one run, half and half along its length: three grand pavilion modules (84 m, the flag block on the middle one) then the Rowley stand's 84 m cut (rowley_end, the same stand shorter, its stair drum at the far end, the lookout near it). His area 4 (the stand-side festival) moves up to x 235..435. Owner, 22:27-22:28: '3, 4 and 5 need aligning neatly. I would then create a gap to 6. We then need more festival bits and pieces between stands. Include that clock building thing?... the clock house that is. You should use this to link stands 1 and 2 maybe and 2 and 3': the joined run (clock house, big pavilion, clock house, three grand pavilions) set at one level (stands.level; each piece had stood at the ground's height under its own origin, so the modules stepped); the clock house (crib 12) linking 1 to 2 and 2 to 3; a 20 m gap before the Rowley stand with festival bits in it (festival kit 'gaps'); stand 1 moved a little towards the bend to make room for the first clock house; his area 4 moved up to x 260..460.
